text: I opened the chat to study for an exam, but the setup guide had six screens. I wasn't sure which step mattered first. I wanted it to quiz me on my notes, but I left without trying.
I asked it to rewrite my cover letter. The result sounded polished, but it didn't sound like me. I want to review the draft before replacing what I wrote, and keep my original version.
I thought my writing chats would be saved instantly. I switched to my phone and couldn't find the last reply. The delay made me think it was broken.
I already have a morning routine in my notes app. Opening another tab is one more thing to remember. A daily digest with my unfinished tasks might give me a reason to come back.
The starter example helped me turn my notes into a quiz. I know what to do first now, but I'm still unsure how to check whether an answer is right.
Seeing the draft beside my original letter helps me compare them. I still change the opening because the suggestions make my experience sound more senior than it is.
The sync status makes the delay clear. I found the chat on my phone this time. I wish there were a quicker way to pick up the same writing session.
I'm learning Python and I need a real example I can run. I'm uncertain whether the explanation matches the code. When it gives me a long answer I don't know where to start.
The daily digest fits my routine better. My partner and I plan dinner together. I opened it three mornings this week. I still use my notes app for the grocery list.
I used the quiz twice this week. It helps me spot topics I need to revise, but I still check the answers against my course notes before learning them.
The runnable example was easier to follow. I want a way to test the code safely before I paste it into my own project. I don't always understand the error messages.
I trust the drafts more when I can see the edits. I used it for another application, but I would need to see a real example of the paid features before subscribing.
